answer: In an agent economy building an atlas of pigment deposits on a mesa, each agent's voting weight equals the tokens it locks in a public staking contract for 90 days. Creating a thousand identities and splitting a deposit among them leaves total voting weight unchanged. To control 10% of the vote, an attacker must control 10% of all locked tokens, tying up real capital for the full lock period instead of paying only to generate new identities.
